The typing correction is made in `goodwatch-webapp/app/server/combined-search/title-lookup.test.ts` only, but I could not run `tsc`, the 139 tests or the build here (no Bash), so it is unverified until you rerun them.

**Cause:** `probe.staged = null` at the start of the test narrows `probe.staged` to `null`. TypeScript does not drop that narrowing across the awaited calls, because the write happens inside the serve stub's evaluated source string. Every later read therefore resolved to `never`, which gives the 10 TS2339 errors.

**Change (three edits):**

1. A typed read accessor directly after `Object.assign(globalThis, { titleLookupProbe: probe })`, with a two-line comment saying why it exists:
   ```ts
   const stagedRanking = (): (typeof probe)["staged"] => probe.staged
   ```
   The return type is the declared property type via indexed access, so it is the exact fixture type (`null | { progress; ranking?; deadline?; deadlineCopy?; completed? }`).
2. In the `try` block: `deadline = probe.staged?.deadline` is now `deadline = stagedRanking()?.deadline`.
3. After the search completes: `const staged = probe.staged` is now `const staged = stagedRanking()`.

Those two reads are the source of all 10 errors: one at the `deadline` read, and nine through the `staged` local (`ranking`, `completed`, `deadlineCopy`, `deadline`, `progress`).

**Unchanged:** `probe.staged = null` still resets the fixture, and the accessor returns the same object reference at runtime, so `assert.equal(staged.deadline, deadline)` and every other assertion compare the same values as before. No stubs, timings, assertions, other tests or runtime source were touched. There is no `any`, `ts-ignore`, cast or new state. I did not touch the V2 snapshot or any other file.

The added lines shift everything below them down by three, so the old 1518–1563 range now sits at 1521–1566 when you compare `tsc` output against the clean base.
